Narrow model spread (typically 23–26°C) stems from stable late-summer steering patterns and modest moisture, aligning with climatological August highs of 20–24°C. Traders assign nearly equal weight to the top two outcomes because small differences in cloud cover thickness or brief wind shifts could determine whether the peak reaches 24°C or stays at 23°C, with higher thresholds remaining unlikely given current observations. Updated model runs and official observations on the 17th will clarify resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: The southwest monsoon, or habagat, currently dominating Luzon has increased cloud cover and rainfall probability over Metro Manila, moderating daytime heating and positioning the market's leading 28–29°C outcomes (combined 81.5% implied probability) as the consensus. PAGASA's extended outlook for August 18 projects a 26–31°C range with 60% rain chances, while ensemble models cluster maxima near 29°C amid typical wet-season humidity and limited solar insolation. These conditions align with climatological baselines for August, where monsoon-driven convection often caps highs below seasonal averages of 30–31°C. Updated model runs and PAGASA briefings in the next 48 hours will refine steering patterns and any intensification of rainfall that could further suppress the daily maximum.
